sodium.options.view_distance.tooltip: The render distance controls how far away terrain will be rendered. Shorter distances mean that less terrain will be rendered, improving frame rates.
sodium.options.simulation_distance.toolt: The simulation distance controls how far away terrain and entities will be loaded and ticked. Shorter distances can reduce the internal server's load and may improve frame rates.
sodium.options.brightness.tooltip: Controls the brightness (gamma) of the game.
sodium.options.gui_scale.tooltip: Sets the maximum scale factor to be used for the user interface. If "auto" is used, then the largest scale factor will always be used.
sodium.options.fullscreen.tooltip: If enabled, the game will display in full-screen (if supported).
sodium.options.v_sync.tooltip: If enabled, the game's frame rate will be synchronized to the monitor's refresh rate, making for a generally smoother experience at the expense of overall input latency. This setting might reduce performance if your system is too slow.
sodium.options.fps_limit.tooltip: Limits the maximum number of frames per second. This can help reduce battery usage and system load when multi-tasking. If VSync is enabled, this option will be ignored unless it is lower than your display's refresh rate.
sodium.options.view_bobbing.tooltip: If enabled, the player's view will sway and bob when moving around. Players who experience motion sickness while playing may benefit from disabling this.
sodium.options.attack_indicator.tooltip: Controls where the Attack Indicator is displayed on screen.
sodium.options.autosave_indicator.toolti: If enabled, an indicator will be shown when the game is saving the world to disk.
sodium.options.graphics_quality.tooltip: The default graphics quality controls some legacy options and is necessary for mod compatibility. If the options below are left to "Default", they will use this setting.
sodium.options.clouds_quality.tooltip: The quality level used for rendering clouds in the sky. Even though the options are labeled "Fast" and "Fancy", the effect on performance is negligible.
sodium.options.weather_quality.tooltip: Controls the distance that weather effects, such as rain and snow, will be rendered.
sodium.options.leaves_quality.name: Leaves
sodium.options.leaves_quality.tooltip: Controls whether leaves will be rendered as transparent (fancy) or opaque (fast).
sodium.options.particle_quality.tooltip: Controls the maximum number of particles which can be present on screen at any one time.
sodium.options.smooth_lighting.tooltip: Enables the smooth lighting and shading of blocks in the world. This can very slightly increase the amount of time it takes to load or update a chunk, but it doesn't affect frame rates.
sodium.options.biome_blend.tooltip: The distance (in blocks) which biome colors are smoothly blended across. Using higher values will greatly increase the amount of time it takes to load or update chunks, for diminishing improvements in quality.
sodium.options.entity_distance.tooltip: The render distance multiplier used by entity rendering. Smaller values decrease, and larger values increase, the maximum distance at which entities will be rendered.
sodium.options.entity_shadows.tooltip: If enabled, basic shadows will be rendered beneath mobs and other entities.
sodium.options.vignette.name: Vignette
sodium.options.vignette.tooltip: If enabled, a vignette effect will be applied when the player is in darker areas, which makes the overall image darker and more dramatic.
sodium.options.mipmap_levels.tooltip: Controls the number of mipmaps which will be used for block model textures. Higher values provide better rendering of blocks in the distance, but could adversely affect performance with resource packs that use many animated textures.
sodium.options.use_block_face_culling.to: If enabled, only the faces of blocks which are facing the camera will be submitted for rendering. This can eliminate a large number of block faces very early in the rendering process, which greatly improves rendering performance. Some resource packs may have issues with this option, so try disabling it if you're seeing holes in blocks.
sodium.options.use_fog_occlusion.name: Use Fog Occlusion
sodium.options.use_fog_occlusion.tooltip: If enabled, chunks which are determined to be fully hidden by fog effects will not be rendered, helping to improve performance. The improvement can be more dramatic when fog effects are heavier (such as while underwater), but it may cause undesirable visual artifacts between the sky and fog in some scenarios.
sodium.options.use_entity_culling.name: Use Entity Culling
sodium.options.use_entity_culling.toolti: If enabled, entities which are within the camera viewport, but not inside of a visible chunk, will be skipped during rendering. This optimization uses the visibility data which already exists for chunk rendering and does not add overhead.
sodium.options.animate_only_visible_text: If enabled, only the animated textures which are determined to be visible in the current image will be updated. This can provide a significant performance improvement on some hardware, especially with heavier resource packs. If you experience issues with some textures not being animated, try disabling this option.
sodium.options.cpu_render_ahead_limit.to: For debugging only. Specifies the maximum number of frames which can be in-flight to the GPU. Changing this value is not recommended, as very low or high values may create frame rate instability.
sodium.options.use_persistent_mapping.to:
For debugging only. If enabled, persistent memory mappings will be used for the staging buffer so that unnecessary memory copies can be avoided. Disabling this can be useful for narrowing down the cause of graphical corruption.

Requires OpenGL 4.4 or ARB_buffer_storage.
sodium.options.chunk_update_threads.name: Chunk Update Threads
sodium.options.chunk_update_threads.tool: Specifies the number of threads to use for chunk building. Using more threads can speed up chunk loading and update speed, but may negatively impact frame times. The default value is usually good enough for all situations.
sodium.options.always_defer_chunk_update: If enabled, rendering will never wait for chunk updates to finish, even if they are important. This can greatly improve frame rates in some scenarios, but it may create significant visual lag where blocks take a while to appear or disappear.
sodium.options.use_no_error_context.name: Use No Error Context
sodium.options.use_no_error_context.tool: When enabled, the OpenGL context will be created with error checking disabled. This slightly improves rendering performance, but it can make debugging sudden unexplained crashes much harder.
sodium.console.game_restart: The game must be restarted to apply one or more video settings!
sodium.console.broken_nvidia_driver:
Your NVIDIA graphics drivers are out of date!
  * This will cause severe performance issues and crashes when Sodium is installed.
  * Please update your graphics drivers to the latest version (version 536.23 or newer.)
sodium.console.pojav_launcher:
PojavLauncher is not supported when using Sodium.
  * You are very likely to run into extreme performance issues, graphical bugs, and crashes.
  * You will be on your own if you decide to continue -- we will not help you with any bugs or crashes!
sodium.console.core_shaders_error: The following resource packs are incompatible with Sodium:
sodium.console.core_shaders_warn: The following resource packs may be incompatible with Sodium:
sodium.console.core_shaders_info: Check the game log for detailed information.
sodium.console.config_not_loaded: The configuration file for Sodium has been corrupted, or is currently unreadable. Some options have been temporarily reset to their defaults. Please open the Video Settings screen to resolve this problem.
sodium.console.config_file_was_reset: The config file has been reset to known-good defaults.
sodium.options.frame_trace.name: Frame Trace
sodium.options.frame_trace.tooltip:
Records what the chunk render path actually does, one row per frame, into sodium-trace.csv in the game directory.

It counts the regions the render walk visits, the sub-draws handed to the driver before and after Sodium's contiguous merge, and the distribution of sub-draws per region, so that optimisation is aimed at a measured bottleneck rather than a guessed one.

This is a measuring instrument, not a performance option: the counters and the CSV write cost time while it is on. Leave it off unless you are collecting data.
sodium.options.frame_trace_window.name: Frame Trace Window
sodium.options.frame_trace_window.toolti: Frames per flush of the trace file, and per summary line in the log. Only used while Frame Trace is enabled.
sodium.options.frame_trace_gl_finish.too:
Also waits for the GPU (glFinish) around every region draw, so the recorded draw time is completion rather than submission.

This serialises the render pipeline and will visibly lower the frame rate: it is for one-off runs that separate CPU time from GPU time, never for judging performance. Only used while Frame Trace is enabled.
sodium.options.flywheel.enabled.name: Enable Flywheel
sodium.options.flywheel.enabled.tooltip:
Draws block entities, models and other virtual geometry as instanced batches through Flywheel's backend, instead of handing them to the renderer one object at a time.

On this device the default backend is instancing, so "on" and "automatic" are the same switch.

Turning it off restores plain rendering and leaves every other setting on this page alone: they are kept and persisted either way, ready for the next time Flywheel is on. Applying this rebuilds the renderer.
sodium.options.flywheel.mobile_driver.to:
Read-only. True when the OpenGL strings identified a mobile or translation-layer driver, which on this device means MobileGlues over a PowerVR GPU.

Flywheel reads this once at startup and uses it to decide which upload and render paths are worth their cost here. It cannot be changed from a settings screen.
sodium.options.flywheel.worker_threads.t:
How many threads precompile Flywheel's shaders.

Automatic (-1) picks a count from the CPU. 0 keeps compilation on the render thread, which is the cheapest in memory and the slowest to get new pipelines ready. A fixed number finishes first use of a pipeline sooner, in exchange for RAM.

The pool is created once and cached for the life of the game, so this one needs a restart: applying it stores the choice, and it takes effect the next time the game starts.
sodium.options.flywheel.limit_updates.to:
Updates objects that are far from the camera on a banded schedule instead of every frame, while nearby ones are still updated every frame.

On by default. Turning it off means every tracked object is rebuilt regardless of distance, which is usually one of the larger CPU costs in a world with a lot of machinery or block entities. Applying this rebuilds the renderer.
sodium.options.flywheel.light_smoothness:
How light is read across a block face.

Flat is the cheapest and bands visibly along edges. Tri-linear interpolates across the face without the inner-face correction. Smooth, the default, follows the face's own geometry. Smooth (inner face corrected) adds a correction that keeps light consistent either side of a solid block.

This is part of the shader key, so changing it recompiles Flywheel's pipelines and applies with a short hitch. Worth settling once rather than flipping.
sodium.options.flywheel.orphan_upload.to:
Uploads an instancer's whole array in one go, instead of patching only the spans that actually changed.

A driver that makes a partial update wait for an in-flight read pays for that stall every frame; measured on this hardware, patching the spans costs several times more than re-uploading at a few thousand instances. Orphaning lets the driver rename the buffer and hand back a fresh one. This is the default on mobile and translation-layer drivers, and is ignored on a desktop driver that renames buffers anyway.

Read inside the upload itself, so it starts working on the next frame with no reload.
sodium.options.flywheel.oit.name: Order-Independent Transparency
sodium.options.flywheel.oit.tooltip:
Renders translucent geometry without draw-order artefacts, using several colour attachments and a few full-screen passes.

On a tile-based GPU each of those passes is a tile load and store, which makes this the most expensive switch on the page. Turning it off renders the same materials as ordinary translucency: cheaper by a wide margin, at the price of the ordering artefacts you would see without it.

The framebuffer belongs to the renderer, so this applies with a reload.
sodium.options.flywheel.disable_particle:
Drops every particle at the source, before it is spawned.

A straight frame-rate trade: no smoke, splash, critical-hit or ambient particles at all. When the GPU is the limit this is one of the largest per-frame wins available.

Takes effect immediately.
sodium.options.flywheel.freeze_gui.name: Freeze GUI Item Animation
sodium.options.flywheel.freeze_gui.toolt:
Stops animated texture frames on items and blocks in the GUI from being re-uploaded while a screen is open.

Opening the inventory normally re-uploads every animated sprite each tick; with this on those uploads pause until the screen closes, and the animation resumes as soon as it does.

Takes effect immediately.
